questions.stem: A seventeen-year-old New Jersey employee completes all study material. What appointment qualification remains?
options: The person must be at least eighteen at appointment
Study lowers the minimum to sixteen
questions.explanation: The manual sets the appointment age at eighteen.
feedback: The qualification is explicit.
Correct. The manual sets the appointment age at eighteen.
Employment does not replace age.
Education does not change the minimum.

questions.stem: A nonresident maintains a New Jersey professional practice. How does the manual treat residence alone?
options: A New Jersey employment or practice connection can support qualification
questions.explanation: The criteria permit the stated New Jersey employment or practice connection.
feedback: Correct. The criteria permit the stated New Jersey employment or practice connection.
The manual expressly provides a nonresident route.
It does not limit it to adjoining states.
Ownership alone is not the listed connection.

questions.stem: A duly qualified Newark notary is asked to serve in Camden. What geographic scope does the manual state?
questions.explanation: A duly commissioned and qualified officer may act throughout the state.
feedback: The scope is statewide.
Employment does not set that territorial restriction.
The provision does not confer worldwide authority.
Correct. A duly commissioned and qualified officer may act throughout the state.

questions.stem: A private school says it can issue a New Jersey commission after payment. Who receives the prescribed state application?
questions.explanation: The manual directs application to the State Treasurer.
feedback: A device seller does not appoint the officer.
A bank manager is not the state commissioning official.
Correct. The manual directs application to the State Treasurer.
A school certificate does not commission the person.

questions.stem: An application is otherwise prepared but lacks its official endorsement. What endorsement does the manual require?
questions.explanation: The application must be endorsed by a member of the Legislature.
feedback: The manual does not name an insurer for this role.
Correct. The application must be endorsed by a member of the Legislature.
A customer is not the specified endorser.
An instructor does not replace legislative endorsement.

questions.stem: An applicant prints an old paper packet and considers that the current filing route. What does the manual require?
options: Electronic application through the provided state means
Only a postal note to a client
questions.explanation: All applications are submitted electronically through the state-provided process.
feedback: Correct. All applications are submitted electronically through the state-provided process.
A vendor fax is not the prescribed filing.
A journal does not apply for appointment.
A client note does not submit the application.

questions.stem: A candidate budgets the manual's commission application fee. Which amount and condition are stated?
questions.explanation: The manual lists a twenty-five-dollar nonrefundable application fee.
feedback: The ordinary act fee is different.
The fee is paid through the state route.
The manual expressly states the charge.
Correct. The manual lists a twenty-five-dollar nonrefundable application fee.

questions.stem: A nonattorney has passed the test but has not completed the Treasurer's course. What prerequisite remains?
options: Proof of completing the required course
questions.explanation: The initial route requires course completion and prescribed examination passage.
feedback: A reference does not replace it.
Supplies do not establish successful study.
Correct. The initial route requires course completion and prescribed examination passage.
A card does not establish education.

questions.stem: An applicant asks what maximum online-test fee the manual authorizes the Treasurer to charge. What is stated?
questions.explanation: The manual states that the Treasurer may charge up to fifteen dollars for each online test.
feedback: The manual expressly allows the stated fee.
Correct. The manual states that the Treasurer may charge up to fifteen dollars for each online test.
That is a different service category.
The listed authority is smaller and per test.
questions.reference: 2026 Manual, Chapter 4, Online testing fee authority

questions.stem: A candidate has watched only the first training video. What education attestation does the current portal require?
options: Reading the manual and watching the entire video series
questions.explanation: The portal requires the complete manual and video-series attestation.
feedback: Correct. The portal requires the complete manual and video-series attestation.
Partial viewing does not match the attestation.
A purchase is not the specified education.
Opening a form does not establish completion.

questions.stem: An applicant already applied for the exam and has attempts remaining. What portal option is identified?
questions.explanation: The portal directs that applicant to its exam-attempt option.
feedback: Renewal is a different process.
The official exam remains required.
An exam attempt does not waive the oath.
Correct. The portal directs that applicant to its exam-attempt option.

questions.stem: An applicant used every exam attempt in the existing application and must retake. What does the portal direct?
options: Assume permanent ineligibility from this page
questions.explanation: The portal directs a new commissioning application for that situation.
feedback: Results belong to the actual applicant.
Passing and qualification precede authorized acts.
Correct. The portal directs a new commissioning application for that situation.
This page supplies a retake route.

questions.stem: A candidate passes the official online exam. What subsequent filing does the portal allow?
options: Transfer the result to another person
Complete and submit the Notary Public Application
Immediately act without the remaining commission steps
Replace the county clerk oath with the score
questions.explanation: The portal says passage allows the registration application to be completed.
feedback: The result is personal.
Correct. The portal says passage allows the registration application to be completed.
Passing is not the entire commissioning process.
The oath remains a later requirement.

questions.stem: An appointee asks the ordinary statutory term length. Which period is stated in the law?
questions.explanation: The statute provides a five-year office term.
feedback: Correct. The statute provides a five-year office term.
That is not the stated New Jersey term.
The term expires.
Acts do not restart it.

questions.stem: A candidate deliberately conceals a material fact in the application. What commission ground does the manual identify?
options: Fraudulent, dishonest or deceitful misstatement or omission
questions.explanation: Dishonest application content can support denial or other commission action.
feedback: Payment does not cure dishonesty.
No busy-applicant exception is stated.
The issue concerns integrity, not formatting.
Correct. Dishonest application content can support denial or other commission action.

questions.stem: A notary applicant has a culpability finding in a state-regulated professional-license proceeding. What should the applicant recognize?
options: A new email account removes the finding
Only criminal convictions may ever matter
The manual lists that disciplinary history among the relevant grounds
questions.explanation: The manual identifies the stated professional disciplinary finding.
feedback: Changing contact details does not alter the finding.
The manual's grounds are broader.
Correct. The manual identifies the stated professional disciplinary finding.
The grounds extend to that history.

questions.stem: A previous notary application was denied in another state. How does the manual treat that history?
options: It can be replaced by a vendor receipt
It is among the stated denial or limitation grounds
It is always irrelevant to New Jersey
It automatically creates a New Jersey commission
questions.explanation: The manual lists other-state denial, nonrenewal and commission limitations.
feedback: A receipt does not change official history.
Correct. The manual lists other-state denial, nonrenewal and commission limitations.
The manual expressly includes the history.
A denial does not issue new authority.

questions.stem: An applicant receives the described adverse-action notice and wants a hearing. What receipt deadline applies to the written request?
options: Twenty calendar days after receiving the notice
Only before the notice is issued
questions.explanation: The manual requires receipt of the request within twenty calendar days.
feedback: Correct. The manual requires receipt of the request within twenty calendar days.
Renewal is not the appeal deadline.
The procedure has a stated limit.
The request responds to a received notice.

questions.stem: An applicant's hearing request says only 'I disagree.' What substance does the manual call for?
options: Detailed reasons, supporting documents if any, and counsel information if represented
questions.explanation: The request describes why the determination is improper and identifies representation.
feedback: An emoji does not explain the challenge.
A stamp does not supply the reasons.
An invoice alone is not the stated request content.
Correct. The request describes why the determination is improper and identifies representation.

questions.stem: An applicant neither files a timely appeal nor preserves the right to appeal. What status does the manual describe for the determination?
questions.explanation: Failure to appeal timely or express waiver makes the decision final under the described procedure.
feedback: It is an agency determination.
It does not renew prior authority.
Correct. Failure to appeal timely or express waiver makes the decision final under the described procedure.
Inaction does not erase the decision.

questions.stem: A newly issued commission is received. Before whom does a resident take and file the qualifying oath?
options: The clerk of the residence county
questions.explanation: The manual directs the resident to the residence county clerk.
feedback: The state route identifies the proper clerk.
Correct. The manual directs the resident to the residence county clerk.
The employer does not perform this filing role.
A trainer is not the designated county clerk.

questions.stem: A renewed commission holder assumes the first term's oath carries over. What does the manual require?
options: Swearing in within three months of receipt of the renewed commission too
questions.explanation: The oath requirement expressly applies to initial and renewed commissions.
feedback: Correct. The oath requirement expressly applies to initial and renewed commissions.
Renewed commissions are included.
A journal cover does not qualify the new term.
A password reset is unrelated.

questions.stem: What official recordkeeping promise is part of the county oath described by the manual?
options: Faithful and honest duties and a true record of legally required matters
questions.explanation: The oath includes faithful duties and truthful required records.
feedback: The office does not guarantee profits.
The oath does not grant attorney authority.
The oath does not approve every document.
Correct. The oath includes faithful duties and truthful required records.

questions.stem: After the oath, what does the clerk cause the notary to endorse?
options: The certificate of commission and qualification
questions.explanation: The manual identifies the commission-and-qualification certificate.
feedback: Marketing does not record qualification.
Bank records do not supply the official certificate.
Correct. The manual identifies the commission-and-qualification certificate.
Supply paperwork is separate.
questions.reference: 2026 Manual, Chapter 4, Commission and qualification certificate

questions.stem: How soon after administering the oath does the manual direct the clerk to transmit the endorsed certificate to Treasury?
questions.explanation: The clerk transmits through the provided electronic method within ten days.
feedback: The manual supplies the deadline.
Correct. The clerk transmits through the provided electronic method within ten days.
That would defeat the stated prompt transmission.
The duty does not depend on a customer.

questions.stem: A recipient never takes the oath within three months. What consequence does the manual state?
options: The Treasurer cancels and revokes the appointment as null and void
Authority continues if the stamp is unused
questions.explanation: The manual states cancellation and revocation for failure within the period.
feedback: Correct. The manual states cancellation and revocation for failure within the period.
The manual provides no automatic extension.
The consequence is substantive.
Unused supplies do not preserve qualification.

questions.stem: A nonresident is regularly employed at a qualifying New Jersey business. Which oath route does the manual describe?
options: The specified New Jersey office or qualifying employer county clerk
questions.explanation: The nonresident route uses the described New Jersey county connection.
feedback: The manual identifies a New Jersey clerk.
Client location does not select this clerk.
The website does not administer that county oath.
Correct. The nonresident route uses the described New Jersey county connection.

questions.stem: A nonresident works from a home office for a business domiciled in New Jersey. Does the manual recognize that employment pattern?
options: Only owning New Jersey land qualifies
Yes, under its specified nonresident conditions
No remote employment can ever qualify
questions.explanation: The manual expressly includes the stated remote-employment arrangement.
feedback: The criterion is the specified employment connection.
The category is not attorney-only.
Correct. The manual expressly includes the stated remote-employment arrangement.
The manual describes that category.

questions.stem: A commissioned nonresident changes the qualifying New Jersey workplace. What subsequent filing is described?
options: An online certificate showing the residence or workplace change
questions.explanation: The nonresident must file the specified change information online with Treasury.
feedback: Customer notice does not update Treasury.
Correct. The nonresident must file the specified change information online with Treasury.
A public post does not file the state certificate.
A sign is not the prescribed filing.

questions.stem: A notary adopts a new name and intends to sign official records in it. What must precede that use?
options: The prescribed signed sworn statement filed with Treasury
Only writing both names on a loose paper
questions.explanation: The manual requires the sworn name-change statement before the described official signing.
feedback: Correct. The manual requires the sworn name-change statement before the described official signing.
Marketing changes do not file the sworn statement.
A customer cannot amend commission evidence.
An unfiled note does not satisfy the process.

questions.stem: A principal offers a driver's license expired two years earlier. How does the manual treat the timing of that listed credential?
options: Every expired license is automatically barred
Expired licenses prove citizenship in every case
It may fall within the no-more-than-three-years expiration allowance
questions.explanation: The listed passport/license/non-driver route permits current credentials or expiration not more than three years before the act.
feedback: The manual expressly allows the stated period.
Identity evidence is not a universal citizenship determination.
The officer applies the identification requirements.
Correct. The listed passport/license/non-driver route permits current credentials or expiration not more than three years before the act.

questions.stem: Another government-issued ID has a facial photograph but no signature and meets the timing condition. What further judgment does the manual require?
options: It is automatically sufficient regardless of the officer's concerns
It must be issued by the stamp manufacturer
It must be satisfactory to the notarial officer
It is always rejected because both features are required
questions.explanation: The alternative route allows signature or photograph and requires officer satisfaction.
feedback: The satisfaction condition remains.
Government issuance is the relevant category.
Correct. The alternative route allows signature or photograph and requires officer satisfaction.
The text uses signature or photograph.

questions.stem: A notary has heard a name often but has no dealings establishing the person's identity. What is required for personal knowledge?
options: Dealings sufficient for reasonable certainty about identity
questions.explanation: Personal knowledge requires sufficient dealings to provide reasonable identity certainty.
feedback: A claimed title does not establish identity.
Correct. Personal knowledge requires sufficient dealings to provide reasonable identity certainty.
A familiar name is not necessarily a known person.
Booking information does not supply those dealings.

questions.stem: A credible witness is personally unknown to the officer. Does the manual provide a way to identify that witness?
options: Yes, with the listed qualifying passport, license or government non-driver ID
No witness can ever be used unless already known
Only the principal's assurance is needed
questions.explanation: The witness may be personally known or identified using the specified credential route.
feedback: Correct. The witness may be personally known or identified using the specified credential route.
The manual gives a documentary alternative.
A receipt is outside that route.
The witness must establish identity through the stated means.

questions.stem: An identity witness offers a casual introduction without a verification oath or affirmation. What is missing?
options: The required sworn or affirmed witness verification
questions.explanation: The route uses verification on oath or affirmation by the credible witness.
feedback: Device details do not provide sworn evidence.
A badge does not administer the verification.
Pricing does not establish identity evidence.
Correct. The route uses verification on oath or affirmation by the credible witness.

questions.stem: A credible witness proposes appearing through compliant communication technology. How does the manual address that possibility?
options: The witness need never appear by any means
Every witness must be physically in the room
It expressly permits that appearance method subject to the stated requirements
questions.explanation: The listed witness route allows personal or communication-technology appearance.
feedback: The witness still appears and gives the required verification.
The manual expressly includes technology appearance.
Correct. The listed witness route allows personal or communication-technology appearance.
Silent email is not the defined communication method.

questions.stem: A listed credential leaves a reasonable identity concern unresolved. What may the notarial officer require?
options: Additional information or identification credentials necessary for assurance
questions.explanation: The manual permits additional identity information or credentials when needed.
feedback: A label does not supply evidence.
Correct. The manual permits additional identity information or credentials when needed.
Payment does not resolve identity.
The list does not remove the officer's assessment.

questions.stem: A principal is identified by a familiar company logo, but no evidence connects the person to the signature. What determination remains?
options: That the appearing person has the claimed identity and the record signature is that person's
That the stamp seller is licensed
questions.explanation: The manual ties the appearing individual's identity to the signature.
feedback: Correct. The manual ties the appearing individual's identity to the signature.
Profitability is outside the identity determination.
Legal enforceability is a different question.
Vendor status does not identify the principal.

questions.stem: The record signature differs substantially from the identification signature, leaving the officer unsatisfied. What does the manual permit?
options: Automatic approval if the client pays
Only copying the old signature onto the record
Refusal based on the stated signature-conformity concern
questions.explanation: Signature conformity is an express refusal criterion.
feedback: Payment cannot remove the concern.
The officer must not alter identification evidence.
Copying a signature does not establish genuine execution.
Correct. Signature conformity is an express refusal criterion.

questions.stem: A signer's appearance does not substantially conform to the ID photo and concerns remain. Which refusal criterion applies?
options: Physical appearance compared with the identification photograph
questions.explanation: The manual expressly includes that physical-appearance concern.
feedback: Furniture is irrelevant.
Impatience does not resolve a mismatch.
Correct. The manual expressly includes that physical-appearance concern.
Paper size does not establish identity.

questions.stem: A confused individual cannot demonstrate understanding of the proposed execution. What authority is stated?
options: The officer must always finish quickly
The officer may refuse when unsatisfied about competence or capacity
The family must decide for the officer
questions.explanation: The manual permits refusal when the officer is unsatisfied about competence or capacity.
feedback: The criterion permits stopping.
Correct. The manual permits refusal when the officer is unsatisfied about competence or capacity.
A relative's preference does not replace the officer's assessment.
Payment does not establish understanding.

questions.stem: An individual appears pressured into signing and the officer is unsatisfied about voluntariness. What does the manual permit?
options: Refusal based on knowing and voluntary execution
Proceeding solely because a manager insists
questions.explanation: Knowing and voluntary signing is an express refusal criterion.
feedback: Correct. Knowing and voluntary signing is an express refusal criterion.
A manager cannot establish the principal's consent.
Ink does not resolve coercion.
The certifying officer retains the assessment.

questions.stem: A remote officer visually checks the Chapter 7 ID but performs no identity-proofing method. What is missing under the manual's stated workflow?
options: One of the specified identity-proofing methods in addition to visual document verification
questions.explanation: The manual lists visual verification and an identity-proofing method together.
feedback: Price does not complete identity.
A receipt is not proofing.
The workflow includes the additional step.
Correct. The manual lists visual verification and an identity-proofing method together.

questions.stem: A principal is shown the answers before answering the identity challenge. What feature is inconsistent with the manual's dynamic-KBA definition?
options: The challenge is an ordinary commission exam
Questions are derived from data sources without providing prior answers
Questions must be about the notary's family
questions.explanation: The definition excludes prior answer provision to the person.
feedback: The definition is broader than payment information.
It is principal identity proofing.
Correct. The definition excludes prior answer provision to the person.
The questions concern identity data.

questions.stem: A remote service uses facial and voice patterns for identity. Which category does the manual identify?
questions.explanation: The manual names facial and voice patterns as biometric examples.
feedback: Posting fees is unrelated to identity technology.
Correct. The manual names facial and voice patterns as biometric examples.
Endorsement concerns an application.
The county oath is a qualification step.

questions.stem: A service proposes using a digital public key certificate as the specified identity-proofing method. Who issues the credential under the definition?
questions.explanation: The manual defines it as an electronic credential issued by a trusted third party.
feedback: Correct. The manual defines it as an electronic credential issued by a trusted third party.
Anonymous self-assertion is not that definition.
Family relationship does not establish the issuer role.
Paper sales do not establish trust-service status.
questions.reference: 2026 Manual, Chapter 8, Digital public key certificate

questions.stem: A principal cannot physically sign and directs the notary to write the principal's name. What does the manual's accommodation require?
options: The officer alone must sign for the principal
Only the employer may direct signing
No explanation of the helper is needed
A directed person other than the notarial officer
questions.explanation: The principal may direct another individual, excluding the notarial officer.
feedback: The text excludes the officer from that signing role.
The direction belongs to the physically unable individual.
The explanatory notation is required.
Correct. The principal may direct another individual, excluding the notarial officer.

questions.stem: A proper helper signs at a physically unable person's direction. What explanation belongs on the record?
options: The helper's name and directing individual's name in the prescribed or similar wording
questions.explanation: The notation explains who affixed the signature and at whose direction.
feedback: Salary does not explain execution.
Study scores do not document the helper's action.
Correct. The notation explains who affixed the signature and at whose direction.
A vague completion note omits the required participants.

questions.stem: A corporate agent acknowledges a record. What does the representative declaration include?
options: Proper authority and signing as the identified entity's act
A guarantee of all company debts
Appointment of the notary as corporate counsel
questions.explanation: The definition includes authorized execution as the represented entity's act.
feedback: The actual appearing person's identity still matters.
Correct. The definition includes authorized execution as the represented entity's act.
The declaration is not a repayment guarantee.
The notary does not become counsel.

questions.stem: A person makes a verification on affirmation. What statement does that act address?
options: That a statement in the record is true
That the customer will win a lawsuit
That the record's market value is high
That the notary drafted the record
questions.explanation: Verification is the individual's sworn or affirmed declaration of record truth.
feedback: Correct. Verification is the individual's sworn or affirmed declaration of record truth.
Litigation success is not the verification.
Market value is not the stated subject.
Drafting is not required by that definition.
questions.reference: 2026 Manual, Chapter 2, Verification on oath or affirmation

questions.stem: A requested certificate says the record was signed or attested before the officer. What service does that form identify?
questions.explanation: The manual provides that signature-witnessing short form.
feedback: Copy certification concerns reproduction.
Endorsement concerns commissioning.
County qualification is different from the customer act.
Correct. The manual provides that signature-witnessing short form.

questions.stem: The remote principal signed one version while the officer holds another. What required determination is missing?
options: Only whether both files are PDFs
Reasonable confirmation that the officer's record is the same signed or statement record
Only whether the file names match
questions.explanation: The manual requires a same-record determination.
feedback: Fees do not establish record identity.
Format alone does not establish content.
Correct. The manual requires a same-record determination.
Similar labels do not establish identical records.

questions.stem: A departing employer claims the journal because it funded the purchase. Whose property does the manual say it is?
questions.explanation: The journal belongs to the notary even when the employer paid.
feedback: A transaction does not transfer the journal.
Correct. The journal belongs to the notary even when the employer paid.
Funding does not change this ownership rule.
The vendor does not own the completed journal.

questions.stem: An employer demands ownership of a paid-for stamping device. What does the manual provide?
options: The device is the notary's property
The client owns it after paying
questions.explanation: The stamping device belongs to the notary despite employer funding.
feedback: Correct. The stamping device belongs to the notary despite employer funding.
The manual expressly addresses employer payment.
Paying an act fee does not transfer the device.
Training does not confer device ownership.

questions.stem: An able notary authorizes a coworker to use the device for independent appointments. What security rule applies?
options: Another person may not use it to perform acts outside the stated physical-inability exception
questions.explanation: The manual limits another person's use to the officer's specific instruction when physically unable to use the device.
feedback: Employment alone does not authorize use.
Customers cannot borrow official authority.
Free work still requires security.
Correct. The manual limits another person's use to the officer's specific instruction when physically unable to use the device.

questions.stem: A notary is physically unable to operate the stamping device. What narrow assistance does the manual describe?
options: The employer takes over the commission
The helper signs every officer certificate
Another person uses it at that notary's specific instruction
An assistant independently conducts all acts
questions.explanation: The exception concerns physical device use under the officer's specific instruction.
feedback: A commission remains personal.
Device assistance does not authorize officer-signature substitution.
Correct. The exception concerns physical device use under the officer's specific instruction.
The exception does not transfer the notarial role.

questions.stem: The stamping device is stolen. Which state notice timing does the manual prescribe?
options: Notify the Treasurer within ten calendar days
questions.explanation: The manual requires Treasury notice within ten calendar days.
feedback: The duty is triggered by loss or theft.
Correct. The manual requires Treasury notice within ten calendar days.
Renewal may be much later.
A supplier notice does not satisfy the state duty.

questions.stem: A journal is lost during an office move. What does the manual require?
options: Treasurer notification within ten days through the indicated contact route
Only a note to the employer
No action until the book is found
questions.explanation: Loss or theft of a journal requires timely Treasury notice.
feedback: Correct. Loss or theft of a journal requires timely Treasury notice.
Replacing the book does not report the loss.
Employer notice alone is insufficient.
The manual imposes a reporting duty.

questions.stem: A filled journal's last act occurred recently, but its first page is old. Which event controls the ten-year retention calculation?
options: The last act chronicled in that journal
questions.explanation: Retention is measured from the last chronicled notarial act.
feedback: The first entry does not set that trigger.
Purchase is not the statutory event.
Manufacturing does not determine legal retention.
Correct. Retention is measured from the last chronicled notarial act.

questions.stem: A notary wants to use the manual's transfer alternative instead of personal retention. What does it direct?
options: Give the book to the last principal
Abandon it at the former office
Write to Treasury for secure-transmission instructions
Mail the book to any vendor
questions.explanation: The manual directs contact with Treasury for secure transmission.
feedback: A client is not automatically an authorized repository.
Abandonment is not a lawful retention plan.
Correct. The manual directs contact with Treasury for secure transmission.
An arbitrary vendor is not the instructed route.

questions.stem: A notary resigns and proposes immediate destruction of the journal. What options does the manual describe?
options: Retain it for the required period or follow Treasury secure-transfer instructions
questions.explanation: Resignation does not eliminate retention or the prescribed transfer process.
feedback: The required transaction record is the journal.
Correct. Resignation does not eliminate retention or the prescribed transfer process.
The manual expressly preserves the record duty.
Customers do not automatically become custodians.

questions.stem: A person knowingly possesses a deceased notary's journal. What manual action is due within forty-five days?
options: Write to Treasury for secure-transmission instructions
Use it for a new personal commission
questions.explanation: The manual directs the representative, guardian or knowing possessor to contact Treasury within forty-five days.
feedback: Correct. The manual directs the representative, guardian or knowing possessor to contact Treasury within forty-five days.
The journal remains a regulated record.
Destruction does not follow the route.
A successor does not inherit the prior officer's journal.

questions.stem: A notary starts one journal for paper acts and another simultaneous journal for electronic acts. What does the manual require?
options: A separate journal for every customer
Only one journal at a time for all acts
questions.explanation: The manual requires one current journal covering tangible and electronic acts.
feedback: Employer convenience does not change that rule.
Electronic acts remain included.
Customer-specific journals would not follow one-at-a-time recording.
Correct. The manual requires one current journal covering tangible and electronic acts.

questions.stem: An officer uses loose sheets with unnumbered lines as the ordinary journal. What physical format is required?
options: A permanent bound register with consecutively numbered lines and pages
questions.explanation: The manual specifies binding, permanence and both line and page numbering.
feedback: Invoices are not automatically that register.
Envelopes do not supply numbered journal entries.
Correct. The manual specifies binding, permanence and both line and page numbering.
Loose scraps omit the prescribed format.

questions.stem: An editable spreadsheet can silently replace completed entries. What journal characteristic must be present?
questions.explanation: Electronic journals must be permanent and tamper-evident.
feedback: Price does not establish compliance.
Correct. Electronic journals must be permanent and tamper-evident.
Decoration does not reveal alterations.
Size does not establish integrity.

questions.stem: An entry records only the month of a service. What transaction timing is required?
questions.explanation: The journal records the date and time of each notarial act.
feedback: Correct. The journal records the date and time of each notarial act.
Commission timing is a different event.
Payment clearing may occur later.
Training does not identify the transaction.
questions.reference: 2026 Manual, Chapter 6, Act date and time

questions.stem: A journal says only 'office visit.' What required classification is missing?
questions.explanation: The manual requires the act type.
feedback: Brand preference does not classify the service.
Employment grade does not identify the act.
A product name is not the legal act type.
Correct. The manual requires the act type.

questions.stem: Two people receive notarial acts, but only the paying person's name and address are entered. What does the manual require?
options: Name and address of each person for whom an act is performed
questions.explanation: The entry requirement extends to each person served.
feedback: Employer data does not replace principal data.
The recipient may not be either principal.
Correct. The entry requirement extends to each person served.
Payment does not limit the requirement.

questions.stem: An officer uses personal knowledge of the principal. What should the journal state?
options: That identity was based on personal knowledge
questions.explanation: The manual requires a statement of that identity basis.
feedback: A file name does not record the route.
Correct. The manual requires a statement of that identity basis.
The entry must reflect actual evidence.
A fee does not record identity evidence.

questions.stem: The principal is identified using a credential. What description does the manual call for when applicable?
options: The method, credential type, issue date and expiration
questions.explanation: The manual identifies those relevant credential details.
feedback: Correct. The manual identifies those relevant credential details.
Color does not supply the stated description.
Style alone does not describe the credential.
A receipt is not the identity evidence.

questions.stem: A credible witness supplies identification evidence. What witness information does the manual identify for the journal?
options: Witness name and signature plus applicable credential details
questions.explanation: The witness route has its own recorded name, signature and applicable identification details.
feedback: A nickname alone is incomplete.
Payment does not identify the witness.
Vendor contact is not witness evidence.
Correct. The witness route has its own recorded name, signature and applicable identification details.

questions.stem: An entry lists only an unexplained grand total for several fees. What format does the manual prescribe?
options: An itemized list of all fees charged for the act
questions.explanation: The manual requires fee itemization.
feedback: Salary is not the transaction's charged fees.
Credit capacity is unrelated.
Correct. The manual requires fee itemization.
Fees are a required entry item.

cards.title: State appointment
cards.front: Who commissions a New Jersey notary?
cards.rule: The State Treasurer commissions the officer through the prescribed electronic application.
cards.boundary: The application requires legislative endorsement.
cards.mixup: A private course certificate does not itself grant office.

cards.title: Initial prerequisites
cards.front: What proof does the nonattorney initial applicant supply?
cards.rule: Successful completion of the Treasurer's required course and prescribed examination.
cards.boundary: The portal directs manual reading, full video-series viewing and attestation.
cards.mixup: Buying study access is different from official completion.

cards.title: Application charge
cards.front: What ordinary commission application fee is stated?
cards.rule: The manual lists a $25 nonrefundable application fee.
cards.boundary: The separate online-test fee authority is up to $15 per test.
cards.mixup: The act fee and application fee are different charges.

cards.title: Personal qualifications
cards.front: What age and state connection are listed?
cards.rule: At least eighteen at appointment, with legal state residence or the stated New Jersey employment or practice connection.
cards.boundary: The applicant must also avoid commission disqualification.
cards.mixup: A New Jersey customer alone does not establish employment or practice.

cards.title: Term and scope
cards.front: How do term and geographic scope combine?
cards.rule: The ordinary statutory term is five years and a qualified officer may serve throughout New Jersey.
cards.boundary: The current manual describes statewide qualified authority.
cards.mixup: A home county is not a county-only practice license.

cards.title: Relevant legal license
cards.front: What defines the manual's nonattorney-applicant category?
cards.rule: An applicant who is not also licensed as an attorney-at-law in New Jersey.
cards.boundary: Another state's legal license does not establish New Jersey licensure.
cards.mixup: A law degree is different from admission to practice.

cards.title: Portal skip
cards.front: Where does the initial portal direct attorneys?
cards.rule: Proceed to the registration-application step.
cards.boundary: The skip instruction concerns the listed examination sequence.
cards.mixup: It does not itself issue a commission or replace the remaining filing.

cards.title: Office still qualified
cards.front: What county step follows an attorney's received notary commission?
cards.rule: The qualifying oath still applies to each initial or renewed commission.
cards.boundary: Professional admission is a separate event.
cards.mixup: Bar admission does not record the commission's county oath.

cards.title: Professional limits
cards.front: Does a notary commission authorize legal practice?
cards.rule: A nonattorney may not claim legal-practice powers from the commission.
cards.boundary: Misleading titles and impressions have their own restrictions.
cards.mixup: Passing a notary exam does not admit someone to the bar.

cards.title: Conflicts remain
cards.front: Does attorney status remove the officer's party-interest prohibition?
cards.rule: The notarial officer's party and direct-beneficial-interest restriction remains applicable as stated.
cards.boundary: The listed restriction includes spouse and civil union partner interests.
cards.mixup: Professional status does not supply a blanket conflict waiver.

cards.title: Active renewal exam
cards.front: What examination rule does the portal state for active renewers?
cards.rule: Active notaries renewing are not required to take the exam.
cards.boundary: The renewal application and applicable education remain separate requirements.
cards.mixup: No-repeat-exam does not mean automatic renewal.

cards.title: Longer lapse
cards.front: What lapse triggers new-applicant exam treatment in the portal?
cards.rule: Expiration more than thirty days earlier triggers the stated new-applicant treatment.
cards.boundary: Do not infer continuing authority from application classification.
cards.mixup: A lapse rule is different from an extension of the old commission.

cards.title: Continuing education
cards.front: What education is described for the manual's qualified renewal category?
cards.rule: The specified continuing-education course is required.
cards.boundary: The current manual omits hour counts appearing in the older announcement.
cards.mixup: Use the current official process without inventing a reconciled duration.

cards.title: No authority cure
cards.front: Can the validity section validate an act performed without authority?
cards.rule: The statute expressly does not validate a purported act by someone lacking acting authority.
cards.boundary: Its duty-omission validity rule has a different scope.
cards.mixup: An old stamp does not supply current office.

cards.title: Post-service records
cards.front: What continues after resignation or suspension?
cards.rule: Journal retention or the prescribed secure-transmission route continues.
cards.boundary: The record period is measured from the last chronicled act.
cards.mixup: Ending current service does not erase historical evidence.

cards.title: Oath window
cards.front: When is the county qualifying oath due?
cards.rule: Within three months after receipt of the initial or renewed commission.
cards.boundary: The oath is taken and filed before the proper county clerk.
cards.mixup: Exam completion does not start a substitute qualification process.

cards.title: Resident clerk
cards.front: Which clerk handles a resident's oath?
cards.rule: The clerk of the county where the notary resides.
cards.boundary: Nonresidents use the separately described New Jersey office/employer county route.
cards.mixup: A client's county does not select this qualifying clerk.

cards.title: Clerk transmission
cards.front: What follows administration of the oath?
cards.rule: The clerk causes endorsement of the commission-and-qualification certificate and transmits it electronically within ten days.
cards.boundary: The notary's three-month oath window is a separate deadline.
cards.mixup: Do not treat the clerk's ten days as the applicant's entire oath period.

cards.title: Missing oath consequence
cards.front: What if the recipient fails to take and subscribe the timely oath?
cards.rule: The Treasurer cancels and revokes the appointment as null, void and ineffective.
cards.boundary: The manual specifies the three-month receipt-based period.
cards.mixup: Unused supplies do not preserve an unqualified appointment.

cards.title: New name evidence
cards.front: What precedes using an adopted new name for official signing?
cards.rule: File the prescribed signed sworn statement explaining the name adoption.
cards.boundary: The statement supplies evidence of continuing powers in the changed name.
cards.mixup: An informal business-card change does not file the state evidence.

cards.title: Party or benefit
cards.front: Which personal interests prohibit the officer's act?
cards.rule: The officer or spouse/civil union partner being a party or having a direct beneficial interest in the record.
cards.boundary: The manual states a violation is voidable.
cards.mixup: Identifying the signer does not cure the independent interest.

cards.title: Advertising notice
cards.front: Which language triggers the manual's advertisement notice?
cards.rule: The manual requires the professional-limit notice with services advertised in any language.
cards.boundary: Use the advertisement's language or the required translation.
cards.mixup: An English advertisement is not excluded by the manual's any-language wording.

cards.title: Client records
cards.front: May an officer withhold a supplied original or photocopy?
cards.rule: The manual identifies withholding access or possession except as allowed by law as an action ground.
cards.boundary: A genuine legal exception must support the withholding.
cards.mixup: An ordinary leverage tactic is not legal authority.

cards.title: Refusal judgment
cards.front: Which concerns support the described refusal?
cards.rule: Competence, capacity, knowing voluntary signing and substantial signature/photo conformity.
cards.boundary: Other law can limit refusal under the stated procedure.
cards.mixup: A customer's payment does not resolve those concerns.

cards.title: Fee categories
cards.front: How does the manual distinguish the listed service fees?
cards.rule: Ordinary listed acts are $2.50, with stated $15 grantor-transfer and $25 mortgagor-financing transaction categories.
cards.boundary: The special real-estate amounts apply regardless of the number of listed services in one transaction.
cards.mixup: A general per-act price is different from a special transaction category.

cards.title: Three-year allowance
cards.front: What timing is stated for the listed identity credentials?
cards.rule: Current or expired not more than three years before the act.
cards.boundary: Other-government-ID acceptance includes its own features and satisfaction requirement.
cards.mixup: An expired credential is not automatically barred or automatically sufficient.

cards.title: Other government ID
cards.front: What features can satisfy the alternative government-ID category?
cards.rule: A signature or facial photograph, within the stated age window and satisfactory to the officer.
cards.boundary: The rule uses either feature, with officer judgment.
cards.mixup: Do not import a both-features rule from another state's law.

cards.title: Credible witness
cards.front: How is the identifying witness known or identified?
cards.rule: The witness appears through the allowed method and is personally known or identified using the listed credentials, with sworn or affirmed verification.
cards.boundary: The witness route is not a casual introduction.
cards.mixup: The notary must establish the witness's own qualifying identity.

cards.title: Extra assurance
cards.front: What can the officer request when evidence leaves uncertainty?
cards.rule: Additional information or identification credentials necessary to assure identity.
cards.boundary: Personal knowledge still requires dealings giving reasonable certainty.
cards.mixup: A document list does not require ignoring a genuine identity concern.

cards.title: Remote proofing
cards.front: What does the manual add to visual remote ID verification?
cards.rule: Use a specified dynamic KBA, biometric or trusted-certificate proofing method under its stated standards.
cards.boundary: Visual display and identity proofing are distinct components.
cards.mixup: A camera image alone does not establish the complete manual workflow.

cards.title: One current journal
cards.front: How are paper and electronic acts chronicled under the ordinary journal rule?
cards.rule: Only one journal at a time chronicles all acts.
cards.boundary: Physical and electronic journal formats are both allowed.
cards.mixup: One simultaneous journal for each medium does not follow that rule.

cards.title: Journal formats
cards.front: What integrity features apply to the journal?
cards.rule: Paper is a permanent bound register with consecutively numbered lines and pages, while electronic form is permanent and tamper-evident.
cards.boundary: An eligible regular-file alternative is separately defined.
cards.mixup: A loose editable note is not the ordinary prescribed journal.

cards.title: Employer-funded property
cards.front: Who owns the employer-funded journal and device?
cards.rule: The manual assigns them to the notary rather than the employer.
cards.boundary: Funding does not change the stated ownership.
cards.mixup: A workplace purchase receipt does not transfer the commission.

cards.title: Loss reporting
cards.front: What reporting period covers journal loss or theft?
cards.rule: Notify the Treasurer within ten days through the stated contact route.
cards.boundary: The manual separately describes device loss/theft with ten calendar days.
cards.mixup: Buying a replacement does not report the missing original.

cards.title: Retention trigger
cards.front: What starts the ordinary ten-year journal period?
cards.rule: The last notarial act chronicled in the journal.
cards.boundary: The manual also supplies a Treasury secure-transmission route.
cards.mixup: The first entry and commission expiration are different dates.

cards.title: Attorney file option
cards.front: What record alternative is available to the stated attorney category?
cards.rule: New Jersey-admitted attorneys may record acts in regularly maintained law-practice files.
cards.boundary: The exception changes the form of records.
cards.mixup: It does not mean keeping no evidence of acts.

cards.title: Attorney employment
cards.front: Which nonattorney connection is included in that alternative?
cards.rule: A notary employed by an attorney-at-law is included.
cards.boundary: Working in the same building is different from employment.
cards.mixup: An ordinary retail employer does not become a law practice by using folders.

cards.title: Licensed title insurer
cards.front: Which title-company roles are described?
cards.rule: Employment by or agency for a title insurer licensed to do business in New Jersey.
cards.boundary: The files regularly maintained for its business record the acts.
cards.mixup: A title-related name alone does not establish the licensed category.

cards.title: Other duties continue
cards.front: Does regular-file recordkeeping remove identity or certificate duties?
cards.rule: The alternative is a record-form option, preserving the other applicable act requirements.
cards.boundary: Remote audiovisual records have separate duties too.
cards.mixup: A file exception is different from an all-purpose exemption.

cards.title: Authorized outside acts
cards.front: How does New Jersey recognize specified acts from elsewhere?
cards.rule: The statute gives the listed authorized other-state, tribal, federal and foreign acts their stated New Jersey effect.
cards.boundary: Apply the actual authority and jurisdiction conditions.
cards.mixup: Recognition does not appoint the outside officer as a New Jersey notary.

cards.title: Advance state notice
cards.front: What precedes first communication-technology work?
cards.rule: Electronically notify Treasury and identify the intended technologies.
cards.boundary: Electronic-record work also has its stated advance notice requirement.
cards.mixup: A provider subscription does not file either notice.

cards.title: Officer location
cards.front: Where does the officer conduct a New Jersey remote act?
cards.rule: The officer is physically located in New Jersey.
cards.boundary: A principal elsewhere is subject to the remaining domestic or overseas conditions.
cards.mixup: The officer's mailing address is not actual physical presence.

cards.title: Remote tangible record
cards.front: What extra process applies when the tangible record is initially elsewhere?
cards.rule: Use the session signing and declaration, sending, recording and post-receipt certificate steps in Chapter 8.
cards.boundary: The officer's possession route for acknowledgment is separately described.
cards.mixup: A scan by itself does not establish every tangible-record condition.

cards.title: Electronic reliability
cards.front: What makes the official electronic credentials reliable?
cards.rule: Uniqueness, independent verification, sole control and tamper-evident record association.
cards.boundary: Limited authorized access disclosures carry their stated conditions.
cards.mixup: A decorative seal image does not establish reliability.

cards.title: Recording evidence
cards.front: What does the manual require for remote recordings?
cards.rule: Create the prescribed audiovisual evidence and retain it for ten years, personally or through a designated repository.
cards.boundary: Standalone remote oaths expressly have recording duties.
cards.mixup: A payment receipt is not the required audiovisual record.

cards.title: Copy determination
cards.front: What does the officer determine about the reproduction?
cards.rule: It is a full, true and accurate transcription or reproduction of the record or item.
cards.boundary: The complete source comparison must support the determination.
cards.mixup: A missing attachment can prevent certification of the entire record.

cards.title: Scope of assurance
cards.front: What does copy certification establish?
cards.rule: Accuracy and completeness of the reproduction of the identified source.
cards.boundary: It does not itself guarantee the source's commercial claims.
cards.mixup: A true copy can reproduce a statement whose merits are a separate issue.

cards.title: Certificate link
cards.front: How is a tangible copy certificate connected?
cards.rule: It is part of or attached to the actual record.
cards.boundary: Electronic association follows its own accurate reliable linkage requirements.
cards.mixup: A loose nearby certificate is not an attached certificate.

cards.title: Certificate timing
cards.front: When is the copy certificate signed?
cards.rule: After the act is performed and contemporaneously with that act.
cards.boundary: The officer also signs and dates the certificate.
cards.mixup: A pre-signed blank for an unknown future copy does not satisfy the sequence.

cards.title: Electronic-to-tangible recording
cards.front: What condition supports the stated original-record satisfaction rule?
cards.rule: The executing officer certifies the tangible copy accurately reproduces the electronic record.
cards.boundary: The statute identifies county clerk, deed-register and surrogate recording offices.
cards.mixup: A printout alone does not supply the required accuracy certificate.

initial-process.summary: Follow the current New Jersey education and examination portal, then complete state appointment and county qualification.

sections.heading: State prerequisites
sections.body: The 2026 manual identifies age eighteen and New Jersey residence or the stated employment/practice connection, subject to disqualification. A nonattorney initial applicant completes the Treasurer's required course and prescribed examination. The current portal directs thorough manual reading, the entire training-video series and the completion attestation. Passing the exam permits the registration application to be completed. It does not finish every appointment step.

sections.heading: Application and verified limits
sections.body: Applications are electronic, endorsed by a member of the Legislature and subject to the stated twenty-five-dollar nonrefundable commission fee. The 2026 manual omits the course-hour figures in the older 2022 announcement. That difference is preserved here without inventing a reconciled duration. Current ordinary exam count, duration and numerical passing threshold remain unconfirmed in the opened official materials. Use the actual official approval and complete the county oath process.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A first nonattorney applicant reads the manual, watches the whole video series and attests to completion, then uses the New Commissioning Application and passes the official test. The applicant completes registration with the required endorsement and payment and later qualifies before the proper county clerk. A commercial badge supplies no appointment authority.

keyFacts: Initial nonattorney applicants complete the required education and prescribed exam.
The portal places the exam before completing registration.
The manual's application fee is $25 and nonrefundable.
Current numerical exam specifications remain unverified.

attorney-exception.summary: Apply the New Jersey attorney instruction to the examination sequence while preserving the remaining commissioning and act duties.

sections.heading: The relevant professional category
sections.body: The manual defines a nonattorney applicant as someone who is not also licensed as an attorney-at-law in New Jersey. A law degree or another state's license does not by itself establish that New Jersey status. The official initial portal directs attorneys to the registration-application step. The instruction addresses the listed examination sequence. An application, appointment and the prescribed county qualification remain distinct administrative matters.

sections.heading: Practice and records boundaries
sections.body: Attorney status does not provide a general waiver of the notarial officer's party or direct-beneficial-interest prohibition. The manual does provide a particular regular-law-practice-files record alternative for New Jersey-admitted attorneys and stated employees. The alternative concerns records form, with other applicable identity, certificate and remote-recording duties preserved. A nonattorney commission grants no legal-advice or immigration-consulting authority.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A lawyer licensed only outside New Jersey examines the manual's definition before claiming the portal exception. The applicant cannot treat a law-school diploma or an attorney friend's license as personal New Jersey admission. An eligible attorney following the skip instruction still completes the proper registration and qualifies the issued commission.

keyFacts: The manual's category turns on New Jersey attorney licensure.
The portal directs attorneys to registration.
The commission's county oath remains a separate requirement.
The regular-file alternative is a records provision.

lapsed-commission.summary: Determine the correct renewal or new-applicant route and preserve the distinction between an application and current acting authority.

sections.heading: Active renewal and a longer lapse
sections.body: The official portal states that active notaries renewing need not take the exam. It treats expiration more than thirty days earlier as a new application requiring the examination. That classification does not state an extension of the old authority. The manual separately requires continuing education for its specified renewal category, including the described prior-course or pre-law appointees. Follow the current portal and education instructions together.

sections.heading: Qualification and historical records
sections.body: An initial or renewed commission requires timely county swearing-in. A missed three-month receipt-based oath period causes the cancellation and revocation described in the manual. Resignation, revocation or suspension also leaves journal-retention or prescribed transmission duties. The statutory validity provision does not validate purported acts by persons without authority, and validity of an act does not bar all challenges to the underlying transaction.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A former notary discovers the commission has been expired more than thirty days. The person follows the portal's new-applicant examination route and stops treating the old stamp as authority. Historical journals remain subject to their retention or transfer requirements while the new appointment process is completed.

keyFacts: Active renewal has the portal's no-exam instruction.
A lapse over thirty days triggers stated new-applicant exam treatment.
The current manual requires applicable continuing education.
Records duties continue after current service ends.

county-oath.summary: Use the proper New Jersey county clerk and complete the commission's receipt-based qualification steps.

sections.heading: Initial and renewed qualification
sections.body: Within three months after receipt of an initial or renewed commission, the notary takes and subscribes the oath before the proper county clerk and files it there. A resident uses the residence county. The manual describes the nonresident route by the specified New Jersey office or qualifying employer county. The oath includes faithful and honest performance and truthful legally required records. Failure within the stated period leads to cancellation and revocation.

sections.heading: Certificates and changed information
sections.body: After administering the oath, the clerk causes the commission-and-qualification certificate to be endorsed and transmits it electronically to Treasury within ten days. Nonresident applicants certify the specified residence and New Jersey employment information and later file changes. Before official signing in an adopted new name, the manual requires the prescribed signed sworn statement explaining the circumstances. Keep these state records aligned with the actual commissioned identity.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A nonresident works remotely for a business whose primary place is in New Jersey. The person verifies the manual's qualifying employment category and proper New Jersey county route, takes the oath within three months of receiving the commission and files later workplace changes. The principal's county is irrelevant to selecting this qualifying clerk.

keyFacts: Both initial and renewed commissions require the timely oath.
The resident route uses the residence county clerk.
The clerk's transmission period is ten days after the oath.
New-name official signing requires the stated prior filing.

conflicts.summary: Screen New Jersey party and benefit restrictions, professional claims, lawful refusal and service-fee categories.

sections.heading: Eligibility for the particular record
sections.body: The manual prohibits an officer's act on a record to which the officer or spouse/civil union partner is a party or has a direct beneficial interest, and states a violating act is voidable. Identity evidence alone cannot remove that independent interest. The manual also regulates nonattorney legal titles and professional-limit notices with advertising in any language. Misleading legal-authority claims and unlawful withholding of client records are commission-action grounds.

sections.heading: Refusal, fees and procedure
sections.body: Chapter 10 permits refusal on the stated capacity, voluntary-execution and signature/photo-conformity concerns, subject to other New Jersey law. Chapter 11 separates ordinary listed acts from its special grantor-transfer and mortgagor-financing transaction fees. Adverse commission action follows the manual's written notice and hearing-request procedure, including the twenty-calendar-day request receipt period. Paying an act fee supplies no waiver of these independent duties.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A principal offers a large fee for a record that directly benefits the officer's civil union partner. The officer recognizes the party/benefit restriction before deciding any price or evaluating signature evidence. A different eligible officer can assess the requested act without the original officer's prohibited interest.

keyFacts: Spouse and civil union partner interests are expressly included.
The manual describes a prohibited-interest act as voidable.
Advertising notice applies in any language under the manual.
Fees do not authorize an otherwise prohibited act.

identity.summary: Apply the manual's identity route and the actual act requirements without importing another state's credential rules.

sections.heading: Personal and documentary evidence
sections.body: Chapter 7 defines personal knowledge by dealings sufficient to give reasonable certainty. Listed passport, license and government non-driver credentials may be current or expired no more than three years. The other-government-ID route permits a signature or facial photograph and requires officer satisfaction. A credible witness gives sworn or affirmed verification, appears through the allowed means and is personally known or identified under the specified credential route. Additional assurance may be requested.

sections.heading: Acts, assistance and remote identity
sections.body: Acknowledgment identity includes the appearing individual and connection to the signature. Verification on oath or affirmation concerns truth of a record statement. A physically unable person may direct someone other than the officer to sign, with the prescribed explanation. Remote work under Chapter 8 uses visual Chapter 7 document verification and the stated proofing method. Signature/photo mismatch, competence or involuntary execution can support refusal under Chapter 10.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A principal presents a government credential with a photograph but no signature. The officer identifies whether the alternative-government-ID category applies, checks its timing and officer-satisfaction conditions and seeks more information if necessary. A rule demanding both features from another state should not replace New Jersey's stated alternative.

keyFacts: The listed expiration allowance is no more than three years.
The other-government-ID category uses signature or photograph plus satisfaction.
The officer may request additional identity assurance.
Remote visual verification and identity proofing have separate roles.

record-ownership.summary: Keep New Jersey notarial property secure and preserve complete records through changes of employer or authority.

sections.heading: Ownership and ordinary journals
sections.body: The manual makes the stamping device and journal the notary's property even when an employer paid. The ordinary journal chronicles all tangible and electronic acts in one current journal, using the prescribed permanent paper or tamper-evident electronic format. Entries identify act time and type, persons served, actual identity evidence and itemized fees. A device's narrow physical-assistance exception does not transfer the notarial role.

sections.heading: Retention and transitions
sections.body: Report journal loss or theft within ten days and device loss or theft within ten calendar days as directed. The journal is retained ten years after its last chronicled act or handled through Treasury's secure-transmission instructions. Resignation or discipline preserves those record obligations. Death or adjudicated incompetency creates a forty-five-day Treasury contact step in the current manual. Electronic credentials and remote recordings have additional control and custody provisions.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A notary leaves an employer that purchased every supply. The officer keeps responsibility for the personal journal and device, identifies the last entry date for retention and maintains electronic access controls. The employer's payment does not justify treating the book as an ordinary disposable departmental file.

keyFacts: The journal and stamping device belong to the notary.
The ordinary rule permits only one current journal.
Journal retention runs ten years from the last chronicled act.
Employer changes do not erase historical records duties.

records-exception.summary: Use the New Jersey regular-file alternative only within its listed professional and business categories.

sections.heading: Eligible records form
sections.body: Chapter 6 permits New Jersey-admitted attorneys, notaries employed by attorneys and the specified employees or agents of licensed title insurers to keep act records in regularly maintained law-practice or title-business files. This is an alternative to the ordinary journal format. An ordinary business does not become eligible simply because it uses folders, and a title-related name does not establish the required insurer license.

sections.heading: Preserved duties and recognized records
sections.body: The alternative still preserves a record of the notarial acts. It does not waive identification, accurate certificates, prohibited-interest screening or Chapter 8 recording requirements. The statute separately recognizes specified authorized acts from other states, tribal jurisdictions, federal authority and foreign jurisdictions. Those recognition provisions have their own authority and jurisdiction predicates and do not issue a New Jersey commission to the outside performer.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A title-insurer agent checks that the insurer is licensed in New Jersey and records actual acts in its regularly maintained business files under the stated category. When the agent also conducts a remote service, the audiovisual evidence is created and retained under Chapter 8. The file alternative alone does not replace that recording.

keyFacts: The exception is an alternative record form.
Qualifying attorney employees are expressly included.
The stated title-insurer category requires licensing.
Other act duties continue to apply.

technology-notice.summary: Follow New Jersey's separate communication-technology and electronic-record requirements for the actual proposed service.

sections.heading: Notice, presence and remote evidence
sections.body: Before first communication-technology work, notify Treasury electronically and identify the intended technologies. The officer remains in New Jersey, with simultaneous secure sight-and-sound communication, same-record confirmation, the prescribed identity workflow and recording. Overseas cases need the stated United States connection and foreign-law condition. The current manual preserves special testamentary laws and describes a limited tangible-record route with its particular conditions.

sections.heading: Tangible and electronic completion
sections.body: Chapter 8 distinguishes acknowledgment when the officer holds the tangible record from the process when it is elsewhere. The latter involves session signing and declaration, sending within three days, recorded signing, post-receipt certificate completion and explanatory wording. Chapter 9 separately addresses advance electronic-record notice, officer technology selection, reliable credentials and tamper-evident association. A subscription does not itself supply any of these legal steps.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A remote principal holds the original paper. The officer chooses the manual's record-not-present process, captures the required signatures and declaration during the session, receives the materials sent within the stated period and completes the required certificate after receipt. An emailed scan alone does not establish that whole procedure.

keyFacts: First remote and first electronic-record work have stated notice requirements.
The remote officer must be in New Jersey.
Remote tangible records have specific alternative workflows.
Electronic credentials must be unique, verifiable, controlled and tamper-evident.

copy-comparison.summary: Certify an actual full and accurate reproduction and connect its certificate to the correct record.

sections.heading: Source and determination
sections.body: Chapter 7 requires determining that the copy is a full, true and accurate transcription or reproduction of the record or item. Missing attachments or altered wording can defeat that determination for the identified source. The copy certificate describes the reproduction, not a commercial guarantee about the source's claims. The short form identifies the relevant record in the named person's possession.

sections.heading: Certificate and electronic copies
sections.body: Complete the act before signing the certificate, with accurate contemporaneous date and the required officer and stamp details. A tangible certificate is part of or attached to its record, and electronic association must be accurate, reliable and tamper-evident. N.J.S.A. 52:7-10.15(c) supplies the stated recording treatment for tangible copies of electronic records when the executing officer certifies copy accuracy. A mere printout does not supply that certification.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A reproduction of a private agreement leaves out the schedule incorporated into the complete source. The officer obtains a full accurate reproduction before certifying the entire agreement, then completes and attaches the correct certificate. A readable stamp cannot cure the missing portion of the copy.

keyFacts: The copy must be full, true and accurate.
The act must precede the officer's certificate signature.
The certificate belongs to the actual identified record.
Electronic-to-tangible recording treatment has a stated accuracy-certification condition.

articles.keyword: two new jersey remote tangible record workflows
articles.intent: Apply New Jersey notarial duties to a specific service scenario
articles.title: Two New Jersey Remote Tangible Record Workflows
articles.description: Distinguish the New Jersey officer-held acknowledgment route from the separate tangible-record-not-present procedure.
articles.h1: Two New Jersey Remote Tangible Record Workflows
articles.lede: The physical location of the paper matters even when the participants meet by video. Chapter 8 describes different procedures for those facts.

sections.heading: Locate the actual record
sections.body: A client wants a remote acknowledgment of a paper record already delivered to a New Jersey officer. The current manual permits the officer to display that tangible record to the remote individual and have the individual identify it during the audiovisual session. This route should be evaluated using the actual held record. The officer should not assume a similarly named file proves that the paper being acknowledged is the same instrument.

sections.heading: Use the different process when paper is elsewhere
sections.body: If the tangible record is not physically before the officer, the manual requires the principal to sign the record and the specified integrated or securely attached declaration during the session. The declaration connects the attached record with the identified notarial act and technology appearance. Merely showing an old signature while promising later delivery does not establish those signing and declaration steps.

sections.heading: Preserve the signing and delivery evidence
sections.body: The officer records the individual signing the record and declaration. The principal sends those materials no later than three days after the act. After receiving them, the officer executes and stamps the certificate and includes the required explanation of witnessing the remote signing. The manual identifies effectiveness by the declaration-signing date, while receipt remains an important completion step.

sections.heading: Keep the remaining conditions
sections.body: Both workflows still require the applicable secure communication, same-record, identity and certificate conditions. The certificate indicates communication-technology use, and the prescribed recording is retained. The manual also preserves special laws governing testamentary instruments while describing its limited tangible-record route. Choosing a paper workflow does not establish that every instrument-specific execution law has been satisfied.
